name: stochastic_reversion_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus
thesis: The Stochastic Oscillator (14,3,3) on 1-min bars identifies when price is near the bottom or top of its recent 14-bar range. When %K crosses above %D in the oversold zone (<20), it signals that downward momentum is exhausting and price is starting to revert from the range bottom. The dual smoothing (3-period SMA on both %K and %D) reduces noise on 1-min bars. The edge exists because the stochastic cross in extreme zones combines two concepts: (1) range position extremity and (2) momentum reversal confirmation. Most traders use stochastics on higher timeframes; on 1-min bars, the signals are faster but also noisier, creating a speed vs accuracy tradeoff that benefits automated execution.
mechanism: Short-term selling exhausts available demand at a price level, creating a temporary liquidity vacuum. Market makers who absorbed the selling begin marking prices back to reduce inventory risk. Limit buy orders resting below create a floor, and new participants entering the long side accelerate the reversion as the forced selling pressure dissipates.

conditions: close > VWAP * 0.995 (not too far below VWAP)
close < VWAP * 1.005 (not too far above VWAP)

exit.signal_exit: exit if stoch_K re-enters extreme zone after crossing out (failed reversion)

weaknesses: Stochastic cross on 1-min bars is extremely noisy — false crosses are frequent, especially with 3-period smoothing
In trending markets, stochastic stays overbought/oversold for extended periods — crosses in extreme zones still fail
Strategy is highly crowded — stochastic is available on every charting platform and widely taught in beginner TA courses
prior_art: Stochastic Oscillator by George Lane (1950s). Standard TA textbook material. The (14,3,3) setting is the default in most platforms. Connors studied stochastic extremes as reversion signals on daily bars. Application to 1-min bars is less documented but common in retail day trading.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
